Allocation-free internal boundary helper uses existing utf8.hpp scalar legality. Strict UTF-16 pairs across native calls, isolated/truncated-unit errors, recovery unit retention, NUL/BOM and encoded scalar remainder for byte-sized reads feed the one Step 25 shared queue.

At most one UTF-16 carry unit and one encoded UTF-8 scalar, guarded by the existing input lease; no second character/line queue. One native UTF-16 unit per input request preserves immediate CR without lookahead. Native console throughput remains unmeasured.

Whole output record validation before native output; invalid console binary returns unsupported/ERROR_NO_UNICODE_TRANSLATION. Bounded 2048-unit chunks and resubmissions contain whole surrogate pairs; no output-size ceiling.

Actual UTF-16 completion counts map to complete source UTF-8 byte progress with original native/cleanup errors. Native acceptance ending after only a high half stops non-retryably and reports Error.partial_utf16_units=1; no duplicated high or isolated low-unit resubmission. Ordinary Operation.write retry respects this fact.

Existing Windows per-request worker/event/targeted-cancellation implementation reused for wide and raw requests. Native conversion/request storage retained until actual completion; no borrowed handle close/replacement, hidden input, mode/code-page/CRT/global signal change.

Shared queue transaction/allocation safety, stdout/stderr whole-record gate, NativeSafe precise-root GC, original request/deadline propagation, cancellation and Runtime carry handoff covered by focused production-helper/adapter tests.

development_failures_and_repairs.review: Ensure a native error accompanying a valid scalar is reported to a partial raw read immediately, while retaining the rest of its UTF8 bytes. Otherwise a control event could be deferred to an unrelated Runtime session.
